newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: E.Asia Oilseeds - S.Koreans back in feeds market.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds - S.Koreans back in feeds market.

text.p: South Korean buyers are expected to return to the feed market to cover their meal requirements for fourth quarter shipments this week, but Japanese firms are holding back on soybean purchases, traders said on Monday.

Earlier Monday South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation (NLCF) said it would invite tenders to buy 40,000 tonnes of soymeal, 10,000 tonnes or 15,000 tonnes of palm kernel meal, and 20,000 tonnes of wheat bran pellet on Tuesday.
Shipment for the NLCF's soymeal tenders was set for between October 4-23 from India or for September 7-26 from South America. Arrival was pegged for November 10 to the three South Korean ports.
"We expect more purchases by other local buyers after the NLCF's tenders on Tuesday," another trader said.
In Japan, some importers are buying U.S. crop for early-October shipments, but most buyers are sidelined at the moment, local traders said.

"We've received orders from some soybean crushers, but most are likely to be quiet this week," a soybean trader at a major trade hoiuse said. "Most players are waiting for better prices and timing to cover new crop U.S. soybeans," he said.
